title: Object Pronouns: Me, You, Him, Her, It, Us, Them
summary: Learn how to use object pronouns in English. These words replace people and things after action verbs.

sections.p: We use subject pronouns like I, he, and she before the verb. But when someone or something receives the action, we use object pronouns like me, him, and her after the verb. They make our sentences shorter and sound much more natural.

ex.en: I love my dog. I feed it every day.
ex.mean: we use 'it' to replace 'my dog' after the verb

ex.en: Sarah is my friend. I like her a lot.
ex.mean: we use 'her' to replace 'Sarah' after the verb

sections.h: Singular Pronouns: Me, You, Him, Her, It
sections.p: Use 'me' for yourself, 'you' for the person listening, 'him' for a male, 'her' for a female, and 'it' for an animal or thing. They always come after an action verb or after prepositions like with, to, or for.

ex.mean: asking another person to help the speaker

ex.en: John is nice. I work with him.
Where is my phone? I need it.
ex.mean: using 'it' to talk about the phone

sections.p: Use 'us' when you and other people receive the action. Use 'them' when two or more people, animals, or things receive the action. Just like the singular pronouns, these always go after the verb or preposition.

ex.en: Our teacher gives us a lot of homework.
ex.mean: the teacher gives homework to the speaker and others

ex.en: Those shoes are cool. I want them.
ex.mean: using 'them' to talk about plural shoes

tip: Think of object pronouns as the receivers of the action. The subject does the action, and the object receives it!

quiz.en: I have a new cat. I love ___ very much.
Can you help ___? I cannot carry this bag.
My parents are cooking dinner for ___.
Look at those birds! Can you see ___?
Tom is my best friend. I play tennis with ___ every weekend.
